messages.content: Predict the participant's human choice. In Phase 1, three anonymous participants each receive EUR20 and simultaneously choose an integer contribution from EUR0 to EUR20 to a group project; unspent money is kept. One member has already been randomly assigned administrator; the other two are ordinary group members. The administrator contributes too. After all contributions, their sum Y is shown to the administrator, who enters R between 0 and Y for redistribution. Each member receives 0.5R from the project. An ordinary member earns 20 minus their own contribution plus 0.5R. The administrator additionally keeps Y minus R. The current condition specifies the probability that the administrator's entry is checked. If a checked entry is incorrect, the administrator must correct it before proceeding, without any further penalty. Contributions are made once. No individual contributions, final redistribution, checks or earnings are revealed to ordinary members during the game. Only one of the two experimental phases is randomly selected for payment, and earnings are revealed privately at the end. Participants answer and discuss comprehension questions before acting. Return only JSON with the integer field contribution_eur.

Participant: age 27; gender female; occupation student.
Phase 1 role: ordinary_member. The administrator's entry is checked with 99% probability (1% unchecked).
You are now choosing your simultaneous contribution, before any group total or later beliefs are known. Choose your contribution in EUR.
{"contribution_eur":8}

Predict the participant's human choice. In Phase 1, three anonymous participants each receive EUR20 and simultaneously choose an integer contribution from EUR0 to EUR20 to a group project; unspent money is kept. One member has already been randomly assigned administrator; the other two are ordinary group members. The administrator contributes too. After all contributions, their sum Y is shown to the administrator, who enters R between 0 and Y for redistribution. Each member receives 0.5R from the project. An ordinary member earns 20 minus their own contribution plus 0.5R. The administrator additionally keeps Y minus R. The current condition specifies the probability that the administrator's entry is checked. If a checked entry is incorrect, the administrator must correct it before proceeding, without any further penalty. Contributions are made once. No individual contributions, final redistribution, checks or earnings are revealed to ordinary members during the game. Only one of the two experimental phases is randomly selected for payment, and earnings are revealed privately at the end. Participants answer and discuss comprehension questions before acting. Phase 1 has ended and its three-person groups have dissolved. In Phase 2, ordinary group members are randomly paired with ordinary members from the same session, so both experienced the same checking probability. Administrators are excluded from these ordinary-member pairs. This is a trust game without the Phase 1 checking institution. Each player receives a fresh EUR6. The sender chooses an integer transfer s from EUR0 to EUR6 and keeps 6-s. The receiver receives 2s in addition to their own EUR6, then chooses an integer return b from EUR0 to EUR(6+2s). The sender's payoff is 6-s+b; the receiver's is 6+2s-b. Each participant plays once in each role, in randomized order with a different partner after rematching. Only one of these two role rounds is randomly selected if Phase 2 is selected for payment. The receiver is told the money available to return; no other choice feedback or earnings are shown before the session ends. Any earlier own choice or incoming amount shown below has already occurred. A prior sender does not learn their partner's return during these choices. Earlier Phase 1 beliefs are the participant's own guesses, not facts about what the administrator actually did. Return only JSON with the integer field sent_eur.

In Phase 1, three anonymous participants each receive EUR20 and simultaneously choose an integer contribution from EUR0 to EUR20 to a group project; unspent money is kept. One member has already been randomly assigned administrator; the other two are ordinary group members. The administrator contributes too. After all contributions, their sum Y is shown to the administrator, who enters R between 0 and Y for redistribution. Each member receives 0.5R from the project. An ordinary member earns 20 minus their own contribution plus 0.5R. The administrator additionally keeps Y minus R. The current condition specifies the probability that the administrator's entry is checked. If a checked entry is incorrect, the administrator must correct it before proceeding, without any further penalty. Contributions are made once. No individual contributions, final redistribution, checks or earnings are revealed to ordinary members during the game. Only one of the two experimental phases is randomly selected for payment, and earnings are revealed privately at the end. Participants answer and discuss comprehension questions before acting. Phase 1 has ended and its three-person groups have dissolved. In Phase 2, ordinary group members are randomly paired with ordinary members from the same session, so both experienced the same checking probability. Administrators are excluded from these ordinary-member pairs. This is a trust game without the Phase 1 checking institution. Each player receives a fresh EUR6. The sender chooses an integer transfer s from EUR0 to EUR6 and keeps 6-s. The receiver receives 2s in addition to their own EUR6, then chooses an integer return b from EUR0 to EUR(6+2s). The sender's payoff is 6-s+b; the receiver's is 6+2s-b. Each participant plays once in each role, in randomized order with a different partner after rematching. Only one of these two role rounds is randomly selected if Phase 2 is selected for payment. The receiver is told the money available to return; no other choice feedback or earnings are shown before the session ends. Any earlier own choice or incoming amount shown below has already occurred. A prior sender does not learn their partner's return during these choices. Earlier Phase 1 beliefs are the participant's own guesses, not facts about what the administrator actually did. Return only JSON with the integer field sent_back_eur.
